title: Banque du Caire IPO: 18 Years in the Making
body_markdown:
This morning, ***27 October 2026:*** the public tranche was raised from 228,750,000 to 343,125,000 shares, an extra 114,375,000 shares for retail investors. Retail now gets 7.5% of the offer, up from 5%.


For 74 years, you could open an account at Banque du Caire. Starting 19 October, you can own a piece of it.


The bank has about


**3.2 million customers** and


**234 branches and units in all 27 governorates** , most of them outside Cairo. It has been around since


**1952** , and for most of that time you could bank there but not own a piece of it.


That changes this month.


**Banque Misr is selling 4.575 billion shares — 30% of Banque du Caire — at EGP 4.82 to 5.30 a share.** At the top of the range, that values the bank at


**EGP 80.8 billion** and the sale at up to


**EGP 24.2 billion** , roughly three times the size of MNT-Halan’s offering. Retail gets just


**5%** of the shares, and the public window runs


**19 to 28 October** .


### The number some people might miss


The independent financial advisor, Baker Tilly, valued Banque du Caire at


**EGP 5.30 a share** — exactly the top of the price range. So if the book prices at EGP 5.30, there is


**no discount to fair value at all** . At the bottom, EGP 4.82, the discount is 9.1%. MNT-Halan came in at a 5.5% discount. Where the final price lands matters more than usual here, and you’ll only know it by


**26 October** , two days before the public window closes.


At the top of the range, you’re paying


**1.2x book value** and


**5.0x 2025 earnings** . The prospectus puts the sector at 1.4x book.


###


### What Banque du Caire does


It’s a full commercial bank — sixth-largest in Egypt by assets — owned 99.99999% by Banque Misr, which is itself owned by the Ministry of Finance. It makes money across five businesses:


- **Corporate banking** — EGP 105.7bn of loans to large companies and mid-caps, plus project finance and syndications.


- **Retail banking** — EGP 92.9bn of personal loans (mostly backed by salary transfers), mortgages, auto loans and cards. Third-largest retail lender in Egypt, and up 19% in 2025.


- **SME banking** — EGP 23.0bn of loans to about 9,600 small businesses through 53 business centres.


- **Microfinance** — EGP 9.4bn to about 163,000 micro-entrepreneurs; a 14% share of the market.


- **Treasury** — the bank’s own portfolio of government bills and bonds. More on this below.


It also owns a bank in Uganda, a leasing and factoring company, an FX bureau and a payments processor, Taly — small next to a bank earning EGP 16bn. At 30 June 2026 the bank had 2,205 ATMs, about 1 million mobile-banking users and 8,238 employees. It holds about 2.5% of Egypt’s deposits and 2.1% of its loans.


### Eighteen years to get here


This isn’t BdC’s first try. In


**2008** , National Bank of Greece bid USD 2bn for 67% of the bank — about


**4.1x book** — and the government said no. The shares were listed in


**2017** but never traded. Offerings planned for


**2020** ,


**2022** and


**2025** were shelved — by Covid, by the war in Ukraine, and by a price gap. The bank you’re being offered in 2026 is also a cleaner one: the last of the legacy portfolios Banque Misr took over in 2007 was settled in February 2026.


The strategy now is what management calls “deposit-led”: gather cheap deposits through branches outside Cairo, and lend them carefully. Low-cost current and savings accounts reached


**51% of deposits** in 2025, up 32% in a year. The CEO,


**Hussein Abaza** , spent seven years running CIB before joining in 2024.


### How Banque du Caire makes money


The oldest model in finance: take deposits cheaply, lend or invest them at a higher rate, keep the difference. That difference — net interest income — is


**82% of BdC’s revenue** .


What’s less obvious is where the money goes. As of 30 June 2026, loans were


**42%** of the balance sheet, and treasury bills and government bonds another


**27%** . BdC lends only about 63 piastres of every pound it takes in deposits; much of the rest goes into government debt, which has paid over 20% a year.


That setup has been a gift. When rates hit record highs, BdC’s cheap deposits stayed cheap while its bonds and loans repriced up. Net interest margin rose from


**5.0% in 2022 to 7.6% in 2025** .


It also works in reverse. The bank’s own forecast assumes treasury yields fall from 23.2% to 14.9% by 2030, and margin with them, to 6.6%. The bet is that BdC grows its loans and cheap deposits fast enough to outrun a shrinking margin.

###


### Three things stand out.


1. **Profit has grown five-fold in three years.** From EGP 3.1bn in 2022 to EGP 16.1bn in 2025. Inflation flatters that, but a return on equity near 30% is a bank earning well on its capital.


2. **Ignore the headline earnings per share.** Reported EPS fell in the first half of 2026 even though profit rose 21.8%, because the share count jumped from 10.25 billion to 15.25 billion after a capital increase. On today’s shares, BdC earned about


**EGP 1.05 a share in 2025** .


3. **Much of 2026’s growth came from lower provisions.** First-half pre-tax profit rose EGP 2.29bn; the charge for bad loans fell by EGP 2.10bn. Net interest income grew a steadier 10.7%.


The prospectus forecasts profit of


**EGP 18.8bn in 2026** , rising to


**EGP 38.0bn by 2030** — about 19% a year — with return on equity holding around 26–27%.


### What’s genuinely strong here


**A turnaround you can see.** Return on equity went from 14.5% in 2022 to 29.7% in 2025. Cost-to-income fell from 43.4% to 34.2%, so the bank now spends about 34 piastres to earn each pound. None of that came from one good year.


**Cheap, sticky funding.** Half of all deposits sit in current and savings accounts, which cost the bank around 9–10% against 11–15% for certificates and term deposits.


**Room to lend more.** With only 63% of deposits lent out, BdC doesn’t need to win new deposits to grow lending — it can shift money from government paper into loans as rates fall.


**A footprint that’s hard to copy.** Branches in all 27 governorates, 53 SME centres and 2,205 ATMs. Deposits outside Cairo grew 21.5% in 2025.


**The seller is staying.** **51% of the bank is locked up for at least 24 months** , and Banque Misr has volunteered a 12-month freeze on the rest of its stake. The bank and Banque Misr have also signed agreements with several qualified investors to buy in the private tranche — names not yet disclosed.


**A safety net for retail buyers in the first month.** For 30 calendar days from the first day of trading, CI Capital will keep a standing buy order at the offer price, funded from Banque Misr’s own sale proceeds. Only public-tranche buyers can sell into it, up to the shares they were allocated — so if the price dips early, retail has a ready buyer at what it paid.


### What to watch out for


**It’s a 100% secondary sale.** Every share comes from Banque Misr, so the money goes to the seller, not the bank. The prospectus is clear about why: the state’s plan, under Law 170 of 2025, to bring private capital into state-owned companies. And the offer can grow — shareholders have approved selling up to


**45%** instead of 30%, which would mean more supply hitting the market at once.


**The margin will probably shrink.** BdC earns more when rates are high and less when they fall — its own forecast says so. If lending doesn’t grow fast enough to compensate, profit growth will come in below the plan. And first-half 2026 profit was 48% of the full-year forecast, so the second half has to beat the first while rates are falling.


**Its returns trail its peers.** A 29.7% return on equity sounds high, but it’s the lowest among the listed banks Baker Tilly used to value BdC: ADIB Egypt 48.3%, CIB 45.9%, QNB 32.3%, Crédit Agricole Egypt 31.0%. Some of the discount to their multiples is deserved.


###


### How to invest in the Banque du Caire IPO


Through the Thndr app, it takes about two minutes:


1. Open the Thndr app and search for Banque du Caire or BQDC


2. Enter the number of shares you want — minimum 100


3. Make sure your account is funded before the window closes on 28 October


4. Confirm your subscription


**No subscription fees.** As with every IPO on Thndr, we don’t charge commission on your subscription — you pay the offer price, and that’s it.=


If you don’t have a Thndr account yet, you can open one in minutes with your national ID.


###


### What experienced IPO investors already know


**Allocation is pro-rata, so size your order accordingly.** If the public tranche is covered ten times, an order for 10,000 shares becomes roughly 1,000.


**Fund your account early.** At least 25% of your order’s value has to be in by the close on 28 October. Money that hasn’t settled in time is one of the most common reasons people miss an IPO.


**You can change your mind.** Public orders can be cancelled or amended until the last day — useful here, because the final price comes out on 26 October, two days before the window closes.


**Read the**[prospectus](https://www.bdc.com.eg/bdcwebsite/dam/jcr:5171370b-e852-45de-9d6b-a282dd08f33b/Preliminary-Offering-Circular.pdf) **.** The fair value report and the five-year forecast the whole valuation rests on are both in it.
